correctness.rationale: The Abrams two-particle cubical inclusion is natural for k≥5 because simple cycles have length at least 3 and essential-vertex separations at least 1. Cell enumeration gives c0=k(k+1)/2, c1=2k(k−1), c2=k(3k−7)/2. For any two-boundary kernel, projection to cells with fixed spoke e yields a graph one-cycle on a path after deleting e endpoints, forcing all two-cells containing spokes to vanish over every field. For a fixed rim edge, the remaining rim partners also form a path, forcing all remaining coefficients zero. The chain complex is connected, whence integral H2=0 and Euler gives H1 rank k+1; injectivity modulo every prime and universal coefficients exclude H1 torsion. Explicit fixed oriented cubical cell counts for identity, rotations, and both reflection conjugacy types yield the signed rim-edge permutation character; finite-group transfer gives quotient rational homology. The embedded checker independently builds boundary matrices and verifies exact ranks and complete D_k traces for k=5..12 (finite corroboration only).

value.rationale: Complete full-symmetry rational homology representation across the infinite canonical wheel graph family is not determined by a Betti rank. Even-rim reflections split into two distinct character classes, and quotient first Betti numbers distinguish cyclic (two rational cycles) from full dihedral (rational acyclicity), with exact formula 1+k/q for subrotation quotients. This naturally resolves symmetry reductions of two-particle graph motions; it is structurally more than a few sampled computations.
